description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Erin Houchin, Republican of Indiana, says she’s “satisfied” with the administration’s briefings to Congress on the war in Iran and stands by President Donald Trump’s approach. Retired Brigadier General Shawn Harris, House Candidate for Georgia (D), discusses the special election to replace Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene and why he believes he has a better chance to win this time.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Warns Against Iran Putting Mines Around Hormuz | Balance of Show: Late Edition 03/10/2026

author: Rachel Metz
description: Anthropic PBC told a judge it could lose as much as billions of dollars in revenue this year and urged quick action on its request to block the Trump administration’s declaration of the company as a US supply-chain risk after a blowup with the Pentagon over artificial intelligence safety issues.
title: Anthropic Tells Judge Billions at Stake If US Shuns AI Tool

description: Retired Brigadier General Shawn Harris, House Candidate for Georgia (D), discusses the special election to replace Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene and why he believes he has a better chance to win this time. He also voices his view on the war with Iran, and why he would support supplemental funding. Ret. Brigadier General Harris speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: 'Everything's Changed': Harris on Georgia Special Election

description: Rep. Erin Houchin, Republican of Indiana, says she’s “satisfied” with the administration’s briefings to Congress on the war in Iran and stands by President Donald Trump’s approach. She acknowledged the conflict would result in a "temporary spike" in gas prices, but expressed optimism that prices would come back down "quickly." Rep. Houchin joined Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Houchin Backs Trump on Iran, Says She’s ‘Satisfied’ With Briefings

description:
On the Big Take podcast, Stacey Vanek Smith and Javier Blas discuss why the global economy is so sensitive to oil price spikes — and how long the impact of even a brief spike can last.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What A $100-Per-Barrel Oil Spike Does To The Global Economy

author: Nathan Risser, Will Kubzansky
description: President Donald Trump said the US will get its first new oil refinery in 50 years with the help of investment from India’s Reliance Industries Ltd.
title: Trump Says US to Get New Oil Refinery With Reliance Backing

author: Matt Shirley
description: Kevin Warsh, President Donald Trump’s pick for Federal Reserve chair, drew praise from a key Republican senator currently blocking his confirmation, but ended a meeting with him without securing a clear pathway forward for his own nomination.
title: Tillis Praises Warsh After Meeting, Yet Won’t Lift Fed Blockade

description: As the conflict extends towards a third week, an arsenal of attack drones and ballistic missiles has helped make Tehran unlike any adversary the US has faced.
title: Iran’s Cheap, Plentiful Weaponry Puts US Military Under Unprecedented Strain

author: Ashleigh Furlong, Kanoko Matsuyama
description: President Donald Trump’s push for lower US drug prices has unexpectedly helped Astellas Pharma Inc. secure higher reimbursement pricing for its new eye medicine in Japan.
title: Trump’s Drug Cost Push Helps Astellas Win Higher Price in Japan

author: Jonnelle Marte, Ben Holland
description: Labor participation for those born in the US has dropped in recent months.
title: Trump’s Border Crackdown Hasn’t Boosted Jobs for US-Born Workers

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Norah Mulinda speak with Bloomberg National Security editor Iain Marlow about the mixed messaging out of the Trump White House around the timeline of the Iran war. Then, Kevin Gordan, Head of Macro Strategy at Schwab, gives his insight about market reaction as oil prices fluctuate. Plus, Bloomberg Balance of Power host Joe Mathieu breaks down the confusion over whether or not the United States escorted an oil tanker through the Straight of Hormuz. Then, Businessweek Daily co-host Tim Stenovec joins the show from the FIA conference in Boca Raton, Florida as he talks to leaders in crypto and prediction markets. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Admin Denies Hormuz Escort, Stocks Whipsawed | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/10/2026

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: Boeing Co. has a new $298 million contract with Israel to deliver as many as 5,000 new air-launched smart bombs, according to three people familiar with the transaction.
title: Boeing Gets $298 Million Israel Deal for 5,000 Smart Bombs

author: Nick Wadhams, Anthony Capaccio
description: President Donald Trump warned Iran against laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz and threatened to blow up any ship attempting to do so, underscoring his determination to get oil flowing through the vital waterway after almost two weeks of war.
title: Trump Warns Iran Against Laying Mines in Strait of Hormuz

description: In just days of attacks, the US has used weapons stores that could take years to rebuild. On today’s Big Take podcast, Sarah Holder sits down with global defense editor Gerry Doyle and Bloomberg Economics’ defense lead Becca Wasser to discuss the arms race that could determine the outcome of the Iran war and what dwindling supplies mean for US readiness moving forward.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War Could Hinge On Who Runs Low On Munitions First

author: K Oanh Ha, Yang Yang (News)
description: On today’s Big Take Asia podcast, we look into the rise and fall of Chen Zhi, the billionaire who allegedly built a criminal network on scams, trafficking and political protection.
title: The Dramatic Rise and Swift Downfall of Alleged Scam Boss Chen Zhi

description:
The US and Iran escalated attacks in the 11th day of the war as oil markets saw fresh volatility and the Trump administration said it’s keeping open additional options to curb spiking energy prices.
Attention continued to be focused on an oil market Tuesday, whipsawed amid the White House’s acknowledgment that a post from US Energy Secretary Chris Wright had erroneously claimed that an oil tanker had been escorted through the Strait of Hormuz. 

“The President and his energy team are closely watching the markets speaking with industry leaders and the US military is drawing up additional options following the President’s directive to continue keeping the Strait of Hormuz open,” White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a briefing.
Bloomberg's Joe Mathieu joins to discuss on BIoomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Denies Navy Escorted Tanker Through Strait of Hormuz

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest developments from Iran. On today's show, Republican Congressman Marlin Stutzman, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Carnegie Endowment for International Peace Senior Fellow Aaron David Miller. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Says It’s Escalating War on Iran | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/10/2026

description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has made clear that when it comes to the Iran war, he’s not done yet. Less clear is President Donald Trump’s willingness to let the conflict drag on much longer.
With the 10-day war roiling oil markets and threatening Republican chances in November’s midterm elections, Trump offered his strongest signal yet on Monday that he’s preparing to de-escalate. His military objectives were “pretty well complete,” Trump said, adding that the conflict would end “very soon.” Aaron David Miller, Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace joins to discussed the unprecedented leverage Trump has over the Israeli Prime Minister.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Has Unprecedented 'Leverage' Over Netanyahu Says Aaron David Miller

author: Nicola M White, Lydia Beyoud
description: The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission plan to coordinate examinations and enforcement for businesses that fall under both agencies’ turf, the latest sign of cooperation between Wall Street’s top regulators.
title: Wall Street Regulators Seek More Enforcement, Exam Coordination

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: The US said no oil tanker has been escorted by its navy through the Strait of Hormuz, refuting an earlier, since-deleted social media post by Energy Secretary Chris Wright.
title: US Didn’t Escort Tanker Through Hormuz, Refuting Wright Post

description:
Navigating the Strait of Hormuz is near impossible with the US and Israeli war against Iran.

Alex Longley explains how new factors like satellite jamming are adding to the danger and confusion. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Weird Shipping Data Adds to Confusion in Strait of Hormuz

author: Aliaksandr Kudrytski, Gerry Doyle
description: Ukraine may face depleted air defenses as the US-led war with Iran burns through global stockpiles of Patriot missiles, the most valuable weapon Kyiv has in its arsenal against relentless Russian attacks.
title: Ukraine Faces Squeeze on Air Defenses as Iran War Burns Supplies

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Mark Niquette
description: President Donald Trump’s efforts to stabilize prices at the pump underscore the unique role oil and gasoline play in the economy — and American voters’ perceptions of it.
title: Spiking Pump Prices Dent Trump’s Willingness to Extend Iran War

author: Melissa Shin
description: Canadian police are investigating a “national security incident” after shots were fired at the US consulate in Toronto early Tuesday morning.
title: Canada Police Investigate Gunfire at US Consulate in Toronto

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US officials signaled military operations were escalating against Iran and there was little chance of diplomatic talks, throwing cold water on President Donald Trump’s suggestion that the conflict could be resolved soon.
title: US Says It’s Escalating War on Iran, Dimming Chance of Talks

author: Damian Shepherd
description: Andy Burnham, the mayor of Greater Manchester and potential leadership challenger to Prime Minister Keir Starmer, said his comments last year that Britain was “in hock” to the bond markets had been “twisted for political reasons,” and blamed successive Westminster governments for failing to boost growth.
title: Burnham Says His Bond Market Remarks Were ‘Twisted for Political Reasons’

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran war has rattled global oil markets. But it’s also raising food and fertilizer prices in a way that could hit poorer countries particularly hard, warned a new United Nations report.
title: Hormuz Disruptions Will Hit Food Prices as Well as Oil, UN Warns

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Switzerland adopts further sanctions against Iran originally issued by the European Union and the United Nations, the government said in a statement.
title: Switzerland Adopts New International Sanctions Against Iran

author: Gerry Doyle
description: Iran’s conventional military has been largely destroyed and it can’t stop US and Israeli air attacks, but the Islamic Republic’s control of the Strait of Hormuz provides a means to escalate the conflict beyond what adversaries may be willing to bear.
title: Iran's Hormuz Control Gives Country Leverage Despite Military Struggles

author: Galit Altstein
description: Israel is set to expand its defense budget by almost 40 billion shekels ($13 billion), about 2% of its gross domestic product, to fund the war with Iran, according to a finance ministry official, who requested anonymity discussing plans that are not yet public.
title: Netanyahu’s Cabinet to Expand Budget by $13 Billion to Fund War

description: Veteran market strategist Ed Yardeni of Yardeni Research says he doesn't see the Iran war stopping anytime soon, but he doesn't see the conflict lasting for months. That's why he sees the risks of a sharp market selloff rising as the war drags on. He speaks on Bloomberg Open Interest about his outlook, gold prices, and where oil is heading.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Yardeni Sees Increased Risk of a Sharp Market Selloff Due to Iran War

author: Peter Martin
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has made clear that when it comes to the Iran war, he’s not done yet. Less clear is President Donald Trump’s willingness to let the conflict drag on much longer.
title: US and Israeli Endgames for Iran Are Diverging as War Drags On

author: Michelle Kaske
description: The agency building a $16 billion rail tunnel under the Hudson River warned Tuesday that construction will halt again within two to three months unless the Trump administration resumes funding, following a February shutdown after the US Department of Transportation withheld promised money.
title: NY-NJ Rail Tunnel Work May Halt Again Without Federal Funds

author: Chris Strohm, Zoe Tillman
description: Ed Martin, a senior Justice Department official and staunch ally of President Donald Trump, is facing allegations of misconduct from attorney ethics regulators in Washington.
title: Trump DOJ Official Faces Disciplinary Proceedings by DC Bar

author: Michael Smith
description: Florida lawmakers who say they want to encourage construction of more affordable housing are trying to strip away powers Miami has used for decades to keep developments, strip malls and warehouses out of the Everglades.
title: Florida Bill Would Open Door to Building More Housing in the Everglades

author: Julian Lee
description: Halt to Black Sea crude shipments offset benefits of soaring prices last week, but they’re coming
title: Russia Set for Oil-Revenue Surge in Coming Weeks on Iran War

author: Colum Murphy, Daniel Flatley, Lucille Liu
description: With three weeks until Donald Trump meets Xi Jinping, Beijing is frustrated by what it sees as insufficient US preparation that may limit the landmark summit to trade agreements and leave key diplomatic and security matters untouched.
title: China Frustrated by Last Minute Scramble to Plan Xi-Trump Summit

description:
The Pentagon said it’s conducting the most intense day of attacks against Iran and won’t give up until the Islamic Republic is defeated, striking a more aggressive tone after President Donald Trump’s suggestion the war could end soon. 
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made the comments during a press conference Tuesday. They suggested the US-Israeli campaign that began on Feb. 28 may still have some way to run, creating further disruption in the oil industry and global markets.   (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Won't End Iran War Until Enemy is Defeated Says Hegseth (Full Presser)

author: Lucy White
description: Nigel Farage reversed his position on the UK’s involvement in the Iran war on Tuesday, saying Britain should not get involved in the conflict.
title: Farage U-Turns to Say UK Shouldn’t Get Involved in Iran War

author: Nicolle Yapur
description: Colombia’s primaries have thrown the May presidential election wide open, reviving hopes for a new market-friendly administration and triggering a rebound in sovereign bonds.
title: Colombia Primaries Upend Election Bets and Fuel Bond Rebound

description: The evidence that Trump doesn’t understand Iran — or its new leader Mojtaba Khamenei — is mounting by the day, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Marc Champion says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Trump Doesn’t Understand About Iran

author: Greg Ryan
description: Massachusetts passed among the fewest laws of any state during the first year of President Donald Trump’s current term, despite having one of the most dominant Democratic majorities in the US.
title: Massachusetts Has Few Laws to Show for Democratic Supermajority

author: Andrea Palasciano, Andra Timu
description: Eastern European countries are making a renewed push to extend NATO’s network of Cold War-era underground fuel pipelines in case of a military conflict, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: NATO Eastern Flank Seeks Extension of Critical Cold War Pipelines

description: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett has told Bloomberg that the objective of the Iran war is to neutralize Iran’s nuclear and ballistic missile capabilities by, metaphorically, cutting off the "head of the octopus," which is the Iranian regime. Speaking to Joumanna Bercetche on "Bloomberg Brief," Bennett said this will take "as long as is necessary."  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Aim of Iran War is to 'Cut Off Head of Octopus': Former Israeli PM Bennett

author: Walter Brandimarte
description: Military interventions in Venezuela and Iran suggest imposing democracy isn’t high on the US leader’s priorities.
title: Trump’s Plans for Cuba Obscure What Comes Next

author: Yian Lee
description: A Taiwanese official said the recent absence of China’s military aircraft near the self-ruled democracy is possibly a move by Beijing to ease tensions ahead of an expected meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
title: Taiwan Links Unexplained Drop in PLA Flights to Xi-Trump Summit

author: Zoltan Simon
description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban capped fuel prices after the poll-leading opposition demanded government intervention before pivotal elections in a month.
title: Orban Caps Fuel Prices After Pre-Election Opposition Pressure

author: Jonnelle Marte
description: One year into President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, there’s little evidence that closed borders are boosting employment for US-born workers.
title: Trump’s Immigration Crackdown Fails to Deliver Jobs for US-Born Workers

author: Eric Martin, Sergio Mendoza
description: The US welcomed Bolivia back to its sphere of influence last weekend by returning a family heirloom to President Rodrigo Paz: the golden cross his father, who was also president, gave to George H.W. Bush in 1990.
title: Bolivia Revives Long-Dead US Alliance at Trump’s Florida Summit

author: Enda Curran, Jorgelina Do Rosario, Daniel Flatley
description: Policymakers around the world are readying measures to absorb surging energy and commodities prices triggered by the Middle East war that now threaten the global economy with its biggest shock since the pandemic.
title: Global Leaders Race to Shield Their Economies From War Shocks

author: Jim Wyss
description: Regime change in Cuba has long been a rallying cry in Miami. Now, with Marco Rubio running the State Department, the powerful political machinery built by Cuban dissidents in Washington is closer than ever to achieving its long-sought dream — just as the militant exile movement that gave rise to it loses strength in Florida.
title: Miami Dissidents Honor Dead From Boat Shootout as Cuba Teeters

author: Sam Dagher
description: Western powers including the US, Australia, France, the UK and others have stepped up efforts to defend their Gulf allies from Iranian attacks, sending additional military assets to the region.
title: Western Powers Rally to Defend Gulf States from Iranian Attacks

author: Michael Nienaber
description: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has persuaded several European partners to club together to provide around 30 PAC-3 guided missiles for Ukraine’s Patriot air-defense systems to bolster dwindling stocks.
title: Germany Helps Procure Scarce Air-Defense Missiles for Ukraine

description:
On today's show, President Donald Trump said he could waive oil-related sanctions, have the US Navy escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz and predicted on Monday that the war with Iran would resolve “very soon” as he confronted mounting economic and political pressure and days of dramatic fluctuations in oil markets.

“I have a plan for everything,” Trump told the New York Post in an interview Monday, referencing the surge in oil prices. “You’ll be very happy.”

Trump also discussed Iran with Russian President Vladimir Putin in their first phone talk this year. Trump said he could waive “certain oil-related sanctions to reduce prices” but didn’t offer additional specifics beyond acknowledging he had discussed the topic with Putin.

Today's guest: Homayoun Falakshahi, Kpler, Head of Crude Oil Analysis; Camille de Courcel, BNP Paribas Markets 360, Head of DM Rates Strategy and Economics, Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Talks to Putin After Iran Market Panic, Insists 'I Have a Plan' | Daybreak Europe 3/10/2026

author: Levin Stamm
description: Swiss arms shipments abroad neared an all-time high last year as European defense spending boomed, in a rebound for an industry that feared extinction over the country’s strict export rules.
title: Swiss Arms Exports Jump as European Defense Spending Booms

author: Kate Sullivan, Arsalan Shahla
description: President Donald Trump on Monday said the US and Israel were making significant progress in their war on Iran and could end the conflict “very soon,” curtailing an oil-price surge.
title: Trump Hints at Early End to Iran War, Easing Oil-Shock Concerns

description: The US, Israel and Gulf states are hoping Iran is running low on missile and drone stocks after data suggested the barrage has slowed since the start of the war on Feb. 28. Iran’s leaders are saying that isn’t the case and they can keep up the war at this intensity for at least six months. Bloomberg Economics Defense Lead Becca Wasser analyzes the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Analysis of Iran's Missile and Drone Capabilities

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Firat Kozok
description: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is deploying an advanced defense system to southeast Turkey after the alliance intercepted two missiles from Iran targeting the nation.
title: NATO to Ramp Up Defense System in Turkey After Iran Missiles

description: Oil tumbled after US President Donald Trump sought to calm markets by saying the Iran war will end soon. Brent and West Texas Intermediate both tumbled more than 10% before clawing back some losses, following a dramatic session on Monday that saw extreme price swings. Bloomberg's Stephen Stapczynski reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil Falls After Trump Says War Will End 'Very Soon'

description: An F/A-18F Super Hornet flies over the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier on March 6. Source: US Navy
title: Oil Prices Cool After Trump Says Iran War Could End 'Very Soon'

author: Jasmina Kuzmanovic, Misha Savic
description: Croatia is resuming mandatory military training after nearly two decades, with the initial recruits joined by far more volunteers than officials were expecting.
title: Renewed Military Draft Sparks Surprise Interest Among Croatia’s Youth

author: Antony Sguazzin, Prinesha Naidoo, Loni Prinsloo
description: South Africa plans to rapidly expand a new credit-guarantee vehicle to support billions of dollars in infrastructure projects, from power-grid expansion and water systems to ports and freight rail.
title: South Africa Targets Infrastructure Deals With Guarantee Fund

author: Randy Thanthong-Knight
description: The Thai government will require most government agencies to adopt full work-from-home arrangements starting immediately as part of its emergency measures to curb energy demand.
title: Thailand Tells State Agencies to Work From Home to Save Fuel

author: Harry Black
description: Finance-sector workers are about to become the unintended beneficiaries of the UK’s Employment Rights Act, a set of trade-union-backed policies primarily designed to strengthen protections for people in low-paying or insecure jobs.
title: Bankers Gain a New Route to Huge Payouts From UK Tribunals

author: Michal Kubala, Andrea Dudik
description: As Russia’s war in Ukraine rages to the east and the US piles on pressure to spend more on the military, Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis has been focusing on a very different agenda.
title: Billionaire Czech Premier Shrugs Off Defense Calls to Focus on Health

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: President Lee Jae Myung said that even if the US military moves air defense assets out of South Korea as the Iran conflict widens, it won’t seriously affect Seoul’s ability to defend itself against nuclear-armed North Korea.
title: South Korea’s Lee Says Security Intact Even if US Weapons Moved

author: Matt Shirley
description: Several Senate Democrats are threatening to force numerous war powers votes and otherwise disrupt the chamber unless Republicans agree to hold public hearings with key Trump administration officials on the reasons for the attacks on Iran.
title: Democrats Vow to Stall Senate Until Trump Team Explains Iran War

author: Aaron Clark
description: Planet Labs PBC is extending its delay on commercial satellite imagery in the Middle East to two weeks from four days over concerns that the intelligence could be used to target North Atlantic Treaty Organization members.
title: Planet Labs Extends Middle East Satellite Imagery Delay on Iran Risks

author: Katrina Manson
description: A top Pentagon official sees little chance of resuming negotiations with Anthropic PBC over military use of its artificial intelligence tools following the company’s legal challenge of an unprecedented government move to declare the firm a supply-chain risk.
title: Pentagon Official Sees Little Chance to Revive Anthropic AI Deal

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Former US Ambassador to NATO Julianne Smith says continued ballistic missile attacks on Turkey could trigger NATO consultations and a potential response. CSIS Middle East Program Director and Senior Adviser Mona Yacoubian says President Trump’s comments that the war is “very complete” suggest an effort to create an economic off-ramp amid concerns a surge in oil prices could disrupt the U.S. economy. President Trump gives a press conference from Florida. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump: Waiving Some Oil-Related Sanctions | Balance of Show: Late Edition 03/09/2026
